toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/bin/sh
# End-to-end for the capture processes without hardware. Usage: capture_e2e.sh <builddir>
#
# Two fake-ld2451 ptys -> real cap-radar and cap-radar-left (the same binary
# under its second name) -> fuse-hub -> store for ~2 s, with junk, bad tails, bad
# lengths, a payload frame and a split frame on the wire; then SIGTERM both
# (exit 0) and verify the log with dlby-logcat, right and left counted apart.
# Also: cap-radar, cap-radar-left and cap-sonar exit 78 when their device is missing.
set -u
B=$1
T=$(mktemp -d /tmp/dlby-capture-e2e-XXXXXX) || exit 1
export DLBY_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
export DLBY_LOG_DIR="$T/log"
hub=""
store=""
fake=""
fake_l=""
radar=""
left=""

cleanup() {
	for p in $radar $left $fake $fake_l $hub $store; do
		kill -KILL "$p" 2>/dev/null
	done
	rm -rf "$T"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

fail() {
	echo "capture_e2e: FAIL: $*"
	for f in "$T"/*.log; do
		echo "---- $f"
		cat "$f"
	done
	exit 1
}

# field <name> <line>: value of name=... in a key=value line.
field() {
	echo "$2" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"
}

# Missing devices are configuration errors: 78, no restart.
DLBY_RADAR_DEV="$T/no-such-tty" "$B/cap-radar" 2>"$T/radar-missing.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-radar with a missing device exited $rc, want 78"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] E open_failed dev=[^ ]+ err=' "$T/radar-missing.log" ||
	fail "no open_failed line from cap-radar"
ln -s "$B/cap-radar" "$T/cap-radar-left" || fail "symlink cap-radar-left"
DLBY_RADAR_LEFT_DEV="$T/no-such-left" "$T/cap-radar-left" 2>"$T/left-missing.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-radar-left with a missing device exited $rc, want 78"
grep -q -E "^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] E open_failed dev=$T/no-such-left err=" "$T/left-missing.log" ||
	fail "cap-radar-left did not use DLBY_RADAR_LEFT_DEV"
DLBY_SONAR_CHIP="$T/no-such-chip" "$B/cap-sonar" 2>"$T/sonar-missing.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-sonar with a missing chip exited $rc, want 78"
grep -q -E '^cap-sonar\[[0-9]+\] E open_failed chip=[^ ]+ err=' "$T/sonar-missing.log" ||
	fail "no open_failed line from cap-sonar"
DLBY_SONAR_TRIG=24 "$B/cap-sonar" 2>"$T/sonar-config.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-sonar with TRIG == ECHO exited $rc, want 78"

"$B/store" 2>"$T/store.log" &
store=$!
i=0
until grep -q ' I start ' "$T/store.log" 2>/dev/null; do
	i=$((i + 1))
	[ "$i" -gt 40 ] && fail "store did not start within 2 s"
	sleep 0.05
done
"$B/fuse-hub" 2>"$T/hub.log" &
hub=$!
i=0
while [ ! -S "$DLBY_RUN_DIR/fuse-hub.sock" ]; do
	i=$((i + 1))
	[ "$i" -gt 40 ] && fail "hub socket did not appear within 2 s"
	sleep 0.05
done

"$B/tools/fake-ld2451" "$T/ttyRADAR" 3 2>"$T/fake.log" &
fake=$!
"$B/tools/fake-ld2451" "$T/ttyLEFT" 3 2>"$T/fake-left.log" &
fake_l=$!
i=0
while [ ! -L "$T/ttyRADAR" ] || [ ! -L "$T/ttyLEFT" ]; do
	i=$((i + 1))
	[ "$i" -gt 40 ] && fail "fake radar ptys did not appear within 2 s"
	sleep 0.05
done

# Both radars' variables are set, as under dlby-super: each must pick its own.
export DLBY_RADAR_DEV="$T/ttyRADAR" DLBY_RADAR_LEFT_DEV="$T/ttyLEFT"
"$B/cap-radar" 2>"$T/radar.log" &
radar=$!
"$T/cap-radar-left" 2>"$T/left.log" &
left=$!
sleep 2
kill -TERM "$radar" || fail "cap-radar already gone"
kill -TERM "$left" || fail "cap-radar-left already gone"
wait "$radar"
rc=$?
radar=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cap-radar exited $rc on SIGTERM, want 0"
wait "$left"
rc=$?
left=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cap-radar-left exited $rc on SIGTERM, want 0"
wait "$fake" || fail "fake-ld2451 exited $?"
fake=""
wait "$fake_l" || fail "fake-ld2451 (left) exited $?"
fake_l=""

sleep 0.2	# let the hub read cap-radar's EOF
kill -TERM "$hub" || fail "hub already gone"
wait "$hub"
rc=$?
hub=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hub exited $rc"
kill -TERM "$store" || fail "store already gone"
wait "$store"
rc=$?
store=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "store exited $rc"

cat "$T"/*.log | grep -q -E 'AddressSanitizer|LeakSanitizer|runtime error' && fail "sanitizer report"
bad=$(grep -v -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] [IWE] [a-z_]+( [a-z_]+=[^ ]*)*$' "$T/radar.log")
[ -z "$bad" ] || fail "malformed log line: $bad"

grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] I radar_up$' "$T/radar.log" || fail "no radar_up"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] W bad_frame reason=tail count=1$' "$T/radar.log" ||
	fail "no bad_frame reason=tail"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] W bad_frame reason=len count=1$' "$T/radar.log" ||
	fail "no bad_frame reason=len"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] I target_frame len=4 hex=f4f3f2f1040001020304f8f7f6f5 count=1$' \
	"$T/radar.log" || fail "no target_frame hex line"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] W radar_silent' "$T/radar.log" && fail "radar_silent while frames flowed"
grep -q -E '^fuse-hub\[[0-9]+\] I sensor_up name=radar$' "$T/hub.log" || fail "hub never saw the radar"
grep -q -E '^fuse-hub\[[0-9]+\] I sensor_up name=radar_left$' "$T/hub.log" ||
	fail "hub never saw the left radar"
grep -q -E "^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] I start dev=$T/ttyLEFT$" "$T/left.log" ||
	fail "cap-radar-left did not open the left device"
bad=$(grep -v -E '^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] [IWE] [a-z_]+( [a-z_]+=[^ ]*)*$' "$T/left.log")
[ -z "$bad" ] || fail "malformed left log line: $bad"
ex_l=$(grep -E '^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] I exit code=0 ' "$T/left.log")
[ -n "$ex_l" ] || fail "no clean exit line from cap-radar-left"
sent_l=$(field sent "$ex_l")
[ "$(field frames "$ex_l")" -ge 8 ] || fail "too few left frames: $ex_l"

ex=$(grep -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] I exit code=0 ' "$T/radar.log")
[ -n "$ex" ] || fail "no clean exit line"
frames=$(field frames "$ex")
sent=$(field sent "$ex")
[ "$frames" -ge 8 ] || fail "too few frames: $ex"
[ "$(field target_frames "$ex")" -ge 1 ] || fail "no target frames counted: $ex"
[ "$(field bad_tail "$ex")" -ge 1 ] || fail "no bad tails counted: $ex"
[ "$(field bad_len "$ex")" -ge 1 ] || fail "no bad lengths counted: $ex"
[ "$sent" -eq "$frames" ] || fail "sent != frames: $ex"

sum=$("$B/tools/dlby-logcat" "$DLBY_LOG_DIR") || fail "dlby-logcat: $sum"
[ "$(field bad "$sum")" -eq 0 ] || fail "bad bytes kept: $sum"
[ "$(field contiguous "$sum")" -eq 1 ] || fail "seq not contiguous: $sum"
[ "$(field radar "$sum")" -eq "$sent" ] || fail "store has $(field radar "$sum") radar records, cap-radar sent $sent"
[ "$(field radar_left "$sum")" -eq "$sent_l" ] ||
	fail "store has $(field radar_left "$sum") left radar records, cap-radar-left sent $sent_l"

echo "capture_e2e: ok (frames=$frames sent=$sent sent_left=$sent_l $sum)"

lines: # (exit 0) and verify the log with dlby-logcat, right and left counted apart.
# Also: cap-radar, cap-radar-left and cap-sonar exit 78 when their device is missing.
+B=$(cd "$1" && pwd) || exit 1	# absolute: the cap-radar-left symlink lives in $T

content.content:
## 1. Architecture

![Architecture: processes, kernel components, hardware, and the rate on every link](docs/architecture.svg)

Seven processes on the Pi 5, all started and watched by `dlby-super`. Sensor data goes
straight to `fuse-hub`, which decides the alert state and forwards a copy to `store`.
Storage is deliberately off the alert path, so a slow SD write can never delay an alert.

| Process | Owner | Role | Scheduling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dlby-super` | Jackson | starts, watches, restarts children | FIFO 90, mostly asleep |
| `cap-radar` | Gage | reads and parses radar frames | FIFO 60 |
| `cap-sonar` | Gage | 60 ms trigger, kernel-stamped echo edges | FIFO 60 |
| `fuse-hub` | Jackson | fusion state machine; own staleness timeout per sensor (radar 3 s, ultrasonic 8 pings, or EOF) | FIFO 70 |
| `alert` | Jackson | LED and buzzer patterns | FIFO 80 |
| `store` | Jackson | power-cut-safe append log | OTHER, nice +5 |
| `status-lcd` | Jackson | bench LCD, kept apart from `alert` | OTHER |

**IPC.** Every link is a Unix domain socket (UDS), `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. Receivers listen on
`/run/dlby/<name>.sock`. Senders reconnect with backoff (50 ms to 1 s) on EOF, `EPIPE`, or
a failed connect (`ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the receiver restarts), so any process can
restart alone. `dlby-super` uses a socketpair per child for heartbeats only. We chose
seqpacket because it keeps message boundaries and reports a dead peer at once as EOF.

**Rates.** The diagram gives the payload and rate on every link. The busiest is
`fuse-hub` → `store` at ~1.1 KB/s (~4 MB/h, ~190 MB per 48 h soak). The radar UART carries
≤1.3 KB/s of its 11.5 KB/s capacity. To confirm on hardware: the ultrasonic rate is
16 Hz, because the HC-SR04 needs ≥60 ms between pings. The
radar message size (~64 B) is an estimate until the LD2451 frame format is checked.
Observed on the bench: with no targets the radar sends one empty frame every ~1.4 s, not
10 Hz ([docs/evidence/sensor-check.txt](docs/evidence/sensor-check.txt)); 10 Hz is assumed
only while it sees targets, unverified.

6:1. **Both sensors flowing through the real pipeline into the store**: cap-radar and cap-sonar,
70:ln -sf /path/to/your/cap-radar ~/dlby-demo/bin/cap-radar
91:export DLBY_CHILDREN=store,fuse-hub,cap-radar,cap-sonar
93:`alert` and `status-lcd` aren't written yet, so `DLBY_CHILDREN` leaves them out. Otherwise
120:dlby-super[…] I child_start name=cap-radar pid=…

lines: ![Architecture: processes, kernel components, hardware, and the rate on every link](docs/architecture.svg)
-Seven processes on the Pi 5, all started and watched by `dlby-super`. Sensor data goes
+Eight processes on the Pi 5, all started and watched by `dlby-super`. Sensor data goes
straight to `fuse-hub`, which decides the alert state and forwards a copy to `store`.
Storage is deliberately off the alert path, so a slow SD write can never delay an alert.
| `dlby-super` | Jackson | starts, watches, restarts children | FIFO 90, mostly asleep |
-| `cap-radar` | Gage | reads and parses radar frames | FIFO 60 |
+| `cap-radar` | Gage | reads and parses radar frames (right radar, UART2) | FIFO 60 |
+| `cap-radar-left` | Gage | the same binary for the left radar (UART4); radar only, no ultrasonic on the left | FIFO 60 |
| `cap-sonar` | Gage | 60 ms trigger, kernel-stamped echo edges | FIFO 60 |
-| `fuse-hub` | Jackson | fusion state machine; own staleness timeout per sensor (radar 3 s, ultrasonic 8 pings, or EOF) | FIFO 70 |
+| `fuse-hub` | Jackson | fusion state machine; own staleness timeout per sensor (each radar 3 s, ultrasonic 8 pings, or EOF) | FIFO 70 |
| `alert` | Jackson | LED and buzzer patterns | FIFO 80 |
| `store` | Jackson | power-cut-safe append log | OTHER, nice +5 |
| `status-lcd` | Jackson | bench LCD, kept apart from `alert` | OTHER |
| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log line |
| radar | dead or unplugged | no valid frame 3 s | DEG; ultrasonic alone | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar` |
+| left radar | dead or unplugged | no valid frame 3 s | DEG; left side unwatched, right side unaffected | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar_left` |
| ultrasonic | dead, unplugged, echo stuck high | no echo edge for 8 pings, or high > 60 ms | DEG; radar alone. Stuck-high needs power cycle | `cap-sonar[413] W sonar_lost reason=no_echo` |
-| both sensors | lost together | both of the above | BLIND | `fuse-hub[415] E blind lost=radar,sonar` |
+| all sensors | lost together | all of the above | BLIND | `fuse-hub[415] E blind lost=radar,sonar,radar_left` |
| `cap-*` process | crash or hang | hub staleness/EOF; super SIGCHLD/heartbeat | hub → DEG at once; super restarts; reconnect restores | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar reason=stale` |
| `fuse-hub` | crash | super SIGCHLD; `alert` silent 1 s | HUB_LOST; restart into BLIND; senders retry on `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` | `dlby-super[400] E child_exit name=fuse-hub signal=SEGV` |
| `alert` | crash, outputs left on | super SIGCHLD | super forces GPIO 17/22 low, restarts | `dlby-super[400] I outputs_forced_off gpio=17,22` |
`alert` and `status-lcd` aren't written yet, so `DLBY_CHILDREN` leaves them out. Otherwise
super would log `code=78` and `child_disabled` for each one.

Run these on the Pi in order, and paste the output after each ✋.

## 1. Check the config, then add UART4
```sh
grep -n -E '^\[|uart' /boot/firmware/config.txt
tail -4 /boot/firmware/config.txt
```
✋ **Expect:** the last section is `[all]`, with `dtoverlay=uart2-pi5` under it. That's the block we added earlier. If so, appending puts the new line under `[all]` too:
```sh
echo 'dtoverlay=uart4-pi5' | sudo tee -a /boot/firmware/config.txt
tail -4 /boot/firmware/config.txt
sudo reboot
```

## 2. After the reboot: is the port there?
```sh
ls -l /dev/ttyAMA*
pinctrl get 12-13
```
✋ **Expect:**
- `/dev/ttyAMA2` and **`/dev/ttyAMA4`**, both in group `dialout`
- `12: … GPIO12 = TXD4` and `13: … GPIO13 = RXD4`

## 3. Is the left radar talking?
```sh
stty -F /dev/ttyAMA4 115200 raw -echo
timeout 6 od -An -tx1 -v /dev/ttyAMA4
```
✋ **Expect:** rows of `f4 f3 f2 f1 00 00 f8 f7 f6 f5`.

If nothing prints, the left radar's TX probably isn't on **pin 33** (GPIO13). Remember TX → RX crosses over: radar **TX** goes to Pi pin **33**, and radar **RX** goes to Pi pin **32**.

## 4. Pull the new code, build, test
```sh
cd ~/dlby-src && git pull && make && make test 2>&1 | tail -3
```
✋ **Expect:** `all tests passed (build)`. Run this **before** any demo `export` lines.

## 5. Link the left radar for the supervisor
```sh
ln -sf ~/dlby-src/build/cap-radar ~/dlby-demo/bin/cap-radar-left
ls -l ~/dlby-demo/bin
```
✋ **Expect:** five links, with `cap-radar` and `cap-radar-left` pointing at the same `build/cap-radar`.

## 6. Quick run with all three sensors
Use one window. Run the exports, start the supervisor in the background, and stop it after 10 seconds:
```sh
export DLBY_RUN_DIR=$HOME/dlby-demo/run DLBY_LOG_DIR=$HOME/dlby-demo/log DLBY_BIN_DIR=$HOME/dlby-demo/bin
export DLBY_CHILDREN=store,fuse-hub,cap-radar,cap-radar-left,cap-sonar
rm -rf ~/dlby-demo/log ~/dlby-demo/run
build/dlby-super 2>&1 | tee ~/dlby-demo/super.log &
sleep 10; kill -TERM $(pgrep -x dlby-super); wait
build/tools/dlby-logcat ~/dlby-demo/log
```
✋ **Expect:**
- `child_start name=cap-radar-left` and `cap-radar-left[…] I start dev=/dev/ttyAMA4`
- `sensor_up name=radar_left`, then `healthy`
- the final line shows `radar=` **and** `radar_left=` above 0, with `bad=0 contiguous=1`

Paste steps 1–3 first. If the left radar is sending frames, the rest should go straight through.

message.content: what does the fuse hub do again?

content.text:
<command-name>/btw</command-name>
            <command-message>btw</command-message>
            <command-args></command-args>
<local-command-stdout>Usage: /btw <your question></local-command-stdout>
what does the fuse hub do again?

`fuse-hub` is the **central process**: every sensor reports to it, and it decides how healthy the system is.

**What it does today:**
1. **Receives sensor messages.** It listens on `fuse-hub.sock` for `cap-radar`, `cap-radar-left` and `cap-sonar`, checks that each message is valid (type and length; for radar, which side), and rejects anything malformed.
2. **Tracks each sensor's health.** It records when each sensor was last heard from:
   - a radar silent for **3s** is lost (`degraded lost=radar` or `radar_left`)
   - the sonar silent for **8 pings (480ms)** is lost
   - a sensor whose process dies (socket EOF) is lost **immediately**

   It then works out an overall state: **OK** (all three up, logged as `healthy`), **DEG** (some lost) or **BLIND** (none up).
3. **Forwards everything to `store`.** Every sensor message is copied unchanged, plus a state record whenever the state changes. If store is down, it counts what it dropped and sends a **GAP** record when store comes back (`store_back dropped=N`).
4. **Heartbeats to `dlby-super`** from its main loop, so a hung hub gets killed and restarted.
5. **Logs stats** every 10 seconds: `stats radar= radar_left= sonar= rejected=`.

**What it doesn't do yet** (Jackson's next work):
- **Fusion**, the APPROACHING and IN_ZONE states. That means using radar targets (range and speed) and confirming them with the ultrasonic. It's blocked on decoding real radar targets, since both radars send `ntargets=0` for now.
- Sending alert states to the `alert` process, for the LED and buzzer.
- Running at SCHED_FIFO priority 70 (Mechanism C).

**Why it's a separate process:** if it crashes, the supervisor restarts it in about 100ms, and the sensors reconnect on their own. That's the `kill -SEGV` scene in your video.

message.content: and what is store for?

content.text:
<command-name>/btw</command-name>
            <command-message>btw</command-message>
            <command-args></command-args>
<local-command-stdout>Usage: /btw <your question></local-command-stdout>
and what is store for?

`store` is the **crash-safe recorder**. It writes everything the hub forwards to disk, so the data survives a power cut. It implements **Mechanism D**, crash-consistent storage.

**What it does:**
1. **Receives from `fuse-hub`:** every sensor message, plus state changes and GAP records.
2. **Appends each one as a record** in `seg-NNNNNN.log` files. Each record has an 11-byte header (length, type, sequence number, **CRC32 checksum**) followed by the message exactly as received.
3. **Syncs to disk:** `fdatasync` at least once a second, and immediately after every state change. A power cut costs at most about 1 second of readings, never a state change.
4. **Recovers on startup:** if the last record is half-written (a power cut mid-write), it **truncates it** (`torn_tail truncated_bytes=N`), continues the sequence numbers and writes a GAP record marking the restart.
5. **Manages space:** 8MB segments, a 512MB cap, and the oldest segment deleted first. If the SD card fills up, it keeps only state changes.

**Why it matters:**
- **In a car, the ignition cuts power without warning.** Without this, the log could end up corrupted, and none of the results could be trusted.
- **It's the project's evidence:** the 48-hour soak test, the evaluation measurements and later replay testing all read this log.
- **It's off the alert path.** It runs at low priority (nice +5), so a slow SD card write can never delay a warning.

**How you see it in the demo:**
- `dlby-logcat` reads the log and checks it.
- **`bad=0`** means no damaged records were kept.
- **`contiguous=1`** means the sequence numbers have no holes.
- On shutdown, the supervisor stops store **last**, so it saves everything the others sent.

message.content: what does the supervisor do?

content.text:
`dlby-super` is the **process that starts and watches every other process**. It's **Mechanism E**, a multi-process design with a supervisor, and its job is to make sure no single failure takes the whole device down.

**What it does:**
1. **Starts the children in order:** `store`, `fuse-hub`, (`alert`, `status-lcd` once they're written), `cap-radar`, `cap-radar-left`, `cap-sonar`.
   - Each child gets a private **heartbeat socket** on fd 3, and nothing else. Every other file descriptor is close-on-exec, so no child inherits stray files or sockets.
2. **Detects crashes.** When a child dies, the kernel sends SIGCHLD. The supervisor receives it through `signalfd` and reaps the child with `waitpid`. That's `child_exit name=fuse-hub signal=SEGV` in your video.
3. **Detects hangs:**
   - Each child must send a heartbeat **every second** from its main loop.
   - No first heartbeat within **10s** of starting, or **5s** of silence after that, gets a **SIGTERM**, then **SIGKILL** 500ms later (`heartbeat_lost`).
4. **Restarts according to exit codes:**

   | How the child ended | What the supervisor does |
   |---|---|
   | exit **0** | It stopped on request: **no restart** |
   | exit **78** (config error, e.g. missing device) | **No restart**, logged as `child_disabled` |
   | **69**, **70**, any other code, or killed by a signal | **Restart** |

   Restarts back off from 100ms, doubling up to 30s, and the delay resets after 60s of healthy running. It never gives up on a sensor.
5. **Takes the children down with it.** Children set `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` and also notice their heartbeat socket closing, so if the supervisor dies, they exit within a second. Nothing is left orphaned.
6. **Shuts down in order.** On SIGTERM it stops the sensors and the hub first, and **store last**, so everything is saved.
7. **Answers to systemd.** It sends `WATCHDOG=1` every second. If the supervisor itself hangs for 3s, systemd kills and restarts the whole service. If systemd hangs, the Pi's **hardware watchdog** resets the board after 15s.

**In your video:**
- **Hub SEGV:** `child_exit … SEGV`, then `child_restart in_ms=100`, a new pid, and `healthy` again.
- **Sonar KILL:** the same pattern, while the hub reports `degraded lost=sonar` in the meantime.
- **Orderly stop:** store exits last, then the supervisor logs `exit code=0`.

**Still to do (Jackson):**
- Real-time priorities: the supervisor at SCHED_FIFO 90, and setting the children's priorities (Mechanism C).
- Forcing the alert LED and buzzer off if `alert` crashes.

**For your defense, know the boundary:** your capture processes **must** call `hb_init`, tick the heartbeat in their loop, and exit 0 on SIGTERM. That's what makes them supervisable.

# M3 demo video: script and walkthrough (Gage)

About 4 minutes on screen. Two Mac Terminal windows side by side, both SSH'd into the Pi:
**T1** (left) runs the supervisor and is never typed into after Step 2; **T2** (right) is
where every command goes.

Type or paste **one command at a time**. Copy only the grey command boxes, never the
"Wait for" or "Say" text. **Never press Ctrl-C in T1.**

---

## Part A: off camera (about 5 min)

**A1. Hardware**
- Pi powered, both sensors wired. Press the HC-SR04 jumpers and the divider leads firmly into
  the breadboard.
- Ultrasonic pointed at a wall or box 0.5–1 m away.
- Both radars wired: **right** radar TX on **pin 29**, **left** radar TX on **pin 33**. Route
  the pin 29 wire so you can pull it **without reaching across the sonar wiring**. Pull it by
  its plastic connector.
- `ls -l ~/dlby-demo/bin` shows a `cap-radar-left` link next to `cap-radar` (same target).

**A2. T1: build and test, before any exports**
```sh
cd ~/dlby-src && git checkout gagebranch && git pull && make && make test 2>&1 | tail -3
```
Wait for: `all tests passed (build)`

**A3. T1: sonar sanity check**
```sh
gpiomon -c gpiochip0 -e both -n 2 24 &
sleep 0.5; gpioset -c gpiochip0 -t 20us,0 23=1; wait
```
Wait for: a `rising` line and a `falling` line. If nothing prints, press Ctrl-C and reseat
the sonar wiring (power off first).

**A4. Both T1 and T2: demo settings**
```sh
cd ~/dlby-src
export DLBY_RUN_DIR=$HOME/dlby-demo/run DLBY_LOG_DIR=$HOME/dlby-demo/log DLBY_BIN_DIR=$HOME/dlby-demo/bin
export DLBY_CHILDREN=store,fuse-hub,cap-radar,cap-radar-left,cap-sonar
```

**A5. T2: nothing left over**
```sh
pgrep -a 'dlby-super|store|fuse-hub|cap-'
```
Wait for: no output. If something is listed, run `pkill -x dlby-super; sleep 2` and check again.

**A6. T1: empty log, clean screens**
```sh
rm -rf ~/dlby-demo/log ~/dlby-demo/run ~/dlby-demo/super.log; clear
```
Then run `clear` in T2. Press ⌘+ in both windows until the text is easy to read.

---

## Part B: recording

Press **⌘⇧5** → **Record Selected Portion** → box both windows → **Options** → your mic →
**Record**.

### Scene 1: intro (T2, ~20 s)
> **Say:** "This is Don't Look Behind You, by Gage Boullosa and Jackson Stokes, for CS370. It's
> a car-mounted blind-spot warning: an LD2451 radar looking back along each side of the car,
> and an HC-SR04 ultrasonic looking sideways on the right. This is milestone 3: both sensors through the real
> pipeline into real storage, with our supervisor mechanism live."

```sh
git log -1 --oneline; ls -l ~/dlby-demo/bin
```
> **Say:** "These links are what the supervisor runs. cap-radar reads a radar over UART, and
> runs twice, once per side; cap-sonar drives the ultrasonic over GPIO. These are the real capture processes, not
> simulated sensors."

### Scene 2: start the system (T1, ~25 s)
```sh
build/dlby-super 2>&1 | tee ~/dlby-demo/super.log
```
Wait for: five `child_start` lines, five `first_heartbeat` lines, `sensor_up` for `radar`,
`radar_left` and `sonar`, then `fuse-hub … I healthy`.
> **Say:** "The supervisor starts the store, the fusion hub, and one process per sensor (the
> right radar, the left radar and the ultrasonic) as separate processes. Each one heartbeats back over its own socket. The hub has seen both
> sensors and reports healthy."

### Scene 3: data reaching storage (T2, ~25 s)
```sh
build/tools/dlby-logcat ~/dlby-demo/log
```
Count to five, then run it again:

#!/bin/sh
# End-to-end for the capture processes without hardware. Usage: capture_e2e.sh <builddir>
#
# Two fake-ld2451 ptys -> real cap-radar and cap-radar-left (the same binary
# under its second name) -> fuse-hub -> store for ~2 s, with junk, bad tails, bad
# lengths, a payload frame and a split frame on the wire; then SIGTERM both
# (exit 0) and verify the log with dlby-logcat, right and left counted apart.
# Also: cap-radar, cap-radar-left and cap-sonar exit 78 when their device is missing.
set -u
B=$(cd "$1" && pwd) || exit 1	# absolute: the cap-radar-left symlink lives in $T
T=$(mktemp -d /tmp/dlby-capture-e2e-XXXXXX) || exit 1
export DLBY_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
export DLBY_LOG_DIR="$T/log"
hub=""
store=""
fake=""
fake_l=""
radar=""
left=""

cleanup() {
	for p in $radar $left $fake $fake_l $hub $store; do
		kill -KILL "$p" 2>/dev/null
	done
	rm -rf "$T"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

fail() {
	echo "capture_e2e: FAIL: $*"
	for f in "$T"/*.log; do
		echo "---- $f"
		cat "$f"
	done
	exit 1
}

# field <name> <line>: value of name=... in a key=value line.
field() {
	echo "$2" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"
}

# Missing devices are configuration errors: 78, no restart.
DLBY_RADAR_DEV="$T/no-such-tty" "$B/cap-radar" 2>"$T/radar-missing.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-radar with a missing device exited $rc, want 78"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] E open_failed dev=[^ ]+ err=' "$T/radar-missing.log" ||
	fail "no open_failed line from cap-radar"
ln -s "$B/cap-radar" "$T/cap-radar-left" || fail "symlink cap-radar-left"
DLBY_RADAR_LEFT_DEV="$T/no-such-left" "$T/cap-radar-left" 2>"$T/left-missing.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-radar-left with a missing device exited $rc, want 78"
grep -q -E "^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] E open_failed dev=$T/no-such-left err=" "$T/left-missing.log" ||
	fail "cap-radar-left did not use DLBY_RADAR_LEFT_DEV"
DLBY_SONAR_CHIP="$T/no-such-chip" "$B/cap-sonar" 2>"$T/sonar-missing.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-sonar with a missing chip exited $rc, want 78"
grep -q -E '^cap-sonar\[[0-9]+\] E open_failed chip=[^ ]+ err=' "$T/sonar-missing.log" ||
	fail "no open_failed line from cap-sonar"
DLBY_SONAR_TRIG=24 "$B/cap-sonar" 2>"$T/sonar-config.log"
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 78 ] || fail "cap-sonar with TRIG == ECHO exited $rc, want 78"

"$B/store" 2>"$T/store.log" &
store=$!
i=0
until grep -q ' I start ' "$T/store.log" 2>/dev/null; do
	i=$((i + 1))
	[ "$i" -gt 40 ] && fail "store did not start within 2 s"
	sleep 0.05
done
"$B/fuse-hub" 2>"$T/hub.log" &
hub=$!
i=0
while [ ! -S "$DLBY_RUN_DIR/fuse-hub.sock" ]; do
	i=$((i + 1))
	[ "$i" -gt 40 ] && fail "hub socket did not appear within 2 s"
	sleep 0.05
done

"$B/tools/fake-ld2451" "$T/ttyRADAR" 3 2>"$T/fake.log" &
fake=$!
"$B/tools/fake-ld2451" "$T/ttyLEFT" 3 2>"$T/fake-left.log" &
fake_l=$!
i=0
while [ ! -L "$T/ttyRADAR" ] || [ ! -L "$T/ttyLEFT" ]; do
	i=$((i + 1))
	[ "$i" -gt 40 ] && fail "fake radar ptys did not appear within 2 s"
	sleep 0.05
done

# Both radars' variables are set, as under dlby-super: each must pick its own.
export DLBY_RADAR_DEV="$T/ttyRADAR" DLBY_RADAR_LEFT_DEV="$T/ttyLEFT"
"$B/cap-radar" 2>"$T/radar.log" &
radar=$!
"$T/cap-radar-left" 2>"$T/left.log" &
left=$!
sleep 2
kill -TERM "$radar" || fail "cap-radar already gone"
kill -TERM "$left" || fail "cap-radar-left already gone"
wait "$radar"
rc=$?
radar=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cap-radar exited $rc on SIGTERM, want 0"
wait "$left"
rc=$?
left=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cap-radar-left exited $rc on SIGTERM, want 0"
wait "$fake" || fail "fake-ld2451 exited $?"
fake=""
wait "$fake_l" || fail "fake-ld2451 (left) exited $?"
fake_l=""

sleep 0.2	# let the hub read cap-radar's EOF
kill -TERM "$hub" || fail "hub already gone"
wait "$hub"
rc=$?
hub=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hub exited $rc"
kill -TERM "$store" || fail "store already gone"
wait "$store"
rc=$?
store=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "store exited $rc"

cat "$T"/*.log | grep -q -E 'AddressSanitizer|LeakSanitizer|runtime error' && fail "sanitizer report"
bad=$(grep -v -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] [IWE] [a-z_]+( [a-z_]+=[^ ]*)*$' "$T/radar.log")
[ -z "$bad" ] || fail "malformed log line: $bad"

grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] I radar_up$' "$T/radar.log" || fail "no radar_up"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] W bad_frame reason=tail count=1$' "$T/radar.log" ||
	fail "no bad_frame reason=tail"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] W bad_frame reason=len count=1$' "$T/radar.log" ||
	fail "no bad_frame reason=len"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] I target_frame len=4 hex=f4f3f2f1040001020304f8f7f6f5 count=1$' \
	"$T/radar.log" || fail "no target_frame hex line"
grep -q -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] W radar_silent' "$T/radar.log" && fail "radar_silent while frames flowed"
grep -q -E '^fuse-hub\[[0-9]+\] I sensor_up name=radar$' "$T/hub.log" || fail "hub never saw the radar"
grep -q -E '^fuse-hub\[[0-9]+\] I sensor_up name=radar_left$' "$T/hub.log" ||
	fail "hub never saw the left radar"
grep -q -E "^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] I start dev=$T/ttyLEFT$" "$T/left.log" ||
	fail "cap-radar-left did not open the left device"
bad=$(grep -v -E '^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] [IWE] [a-z_]+( [a-z_]+=[^ ]*)*$' "$T/left.log")
[ -z "$bad" ] || fail "malformed left log line: $bad"
ex_l=$(grep -E '^cap-radar-left\[[0-9]+\] I exit code=0 ' "$T/left.log")
[ -n "$ex_l" ] || fail "no clean exit line from cap-radar-left"
sent_l=$(field sent "$ex_l")
[ "$(field frames "$ex_l")" -ge 8 ] || fail "too few left frames: $ex_l"

ex=$(grep -E '^cap-radar\[[0-9]+\] I exit code=0 ' "$T/radar.log")
[ -n "$ex" ] || fail "no clean exit line"
frames=$(field frames "$ex")
sent=$(field sent "$ex")
[ "$frames" -ge 8 ] || fail "too few frames: $ex"
[ "$(field target_frames "$ex")" -ge 1 ] || fail "no target frames counted: $ex"
[ "$(field bad_tail "$ex")" -ge 1 ] || fail "no bad tails counted: $ex"
[ "$(field bad_len "$ex")" -ge 1 ] || fail "no bad lengths counted: $ex"
[ "$sent" -eq "$frames" ] || fail "sent != frames: $ex"

sum=$("$B/tools/dlby-logcat" "$DLBY_LOG_DIR") || fail "dlby-logcat: $sum"
[ "$(field bad "$sum")" -eq 0 ] || fail "bad bytes kept: $sum"
[ "$(field contiguous "$sum")" -eq 1 ] || fail "seq not contiguous: $sum"
[ "$(field radar "$sum")" -eq "$sent" ] || fail "store has $(field radar "$sum") radar records, cap-radar sent $sent"
[ "$(field radar_left "$sum")" -eq "$sent_l" ] ||
	fail "store has $(field radar_left "$sum") left radar records, cap-radar-left sent $sent_l"

echo "capture_e2e: ok (frames=$frames sent=$sent sent_left=$sent_l $sum)"

#!/bin/sh
# End-to-end for dlby-super (DESIGN.md §2 E, §3, §6 "E restart"). Usage: super_e2e.sh <builddir>
#
# Children: the real store and fuse-hub; fake-sensors as cap-sonar and cap-radar-left,
# so real sonar and left-radar data flows -> fuse-hub -> store; fake-child as alert
# (crashes once at 1 s), status-lcd (exits 78) and cap-radar (hangs once at 1 s,
# ignoring SIGTERM).
#
# Phase 1, one super:
#   start order and first heartbeats; kill -SEGV fuse-hub -> new hub within 1 s and
#   sonar keeps reaching store; kill -KILL store -> restarted; alert crash -> restart;
#   status-lcd 78 -> disabled; cap-radar hang -> heartbeat_lost, KILL, restart;
#   inherited fds only 0-3; TERM super -> store stopped last, exit 0, no child left.
# Phase 2: kill -KILL super -> every child exits within 1 s (PDEATHSIG, hb EOF).
set -u
B=$(cd "$1" && pwd) || exit 1
T=$(mktemp -d /tmp/dlby-super-e2e-XXXXXX) || exit 1
export DLBY_RUN_DIR="$T/run" DLBY_LOG_DIR="$T/log" DLBY_BIN_DIR="$T/bin" FAKE_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
export FAKE_alert=crash_once:1 FAKE_status_lcd=exit:78 FAKE_cap_radar=hang_once:1
# The SIGSEGVs here are intentional (fake alert, kill -SEGV on the hub): they must
# kill by signal as in production, not become an ASan report and exit 1. Only this
# test sets it; ASan's memory checks stay on.
export ASAN_OPTIONS="${ASAN_OPTIONS:+$ASAN_OPTIONS:}handle_segv=0"
LOG="$T/super1.log"
LOG2="$T/super2.log"
super=""

# Every child pid either super started.
all_pids() {
	cat "$LOG" "$LOG2" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^dlby-super\[[0-9]*\] I child_start name=[^ ]* pid=//p'
}

cleanup() {
	[ -n "$super" ] && kill -KILL "$super" 2>/dev/null
	for p in $(all_pids); do
		kill -KILL "$p" 2>/dev/null
	done
	rm -rf "$T"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

fail() {
	echo "super_e2e: FAIL: $*"
	for f in "$LOG" "$LOG2"; do
		[ -f "$f" ] || continue
		echo "---- $f"
		cat "$f"
	done
	exit 1
}

# wait_for <regex> <file> <timeout_ms>
wait_for() {
	i=0
	while ! grep -q -E "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null; do
		i=$((i + 1))
		[ "$i" -gt $(($3 / 20)) ] && return 1
		sleep 0.02
	done
}

count() {
	grep -c -E "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
}

# wait_count <regex> <file> <n> <timeout_ms>
wait_count() {
	i=0
	while [ "$(count "$1" "$2")" -lt "$3" ]; do
		i=$((i + 1))
		[ "$i" -gt $(($4 / 20)) ] && return 1
		sleep 0.02
	done
}

pid_of() {
	sed -n "s/^dlby-super\[[0-9]*\] I child_start name=$1 pid=//p" "$2" | tail -n 1
}

field() {
	echo "$2" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"
}

# Running and not a zombie (orphans may never be reaped inside a container).
alive() {
	[ -r "/proc/$1/stat" ] || return 1
	s=$(sed -n 's/^[0-9]* (.*) \(.\) .*/\1/p' "/proc/$1/stat" 2>/dev/null)
	[ -n "$s" ] && [ "$s" != Z ]
}

sonar_records() {
	field sonar "$("$B/tools/dlby-logcat" "$DLBY_LOG_DIR" 2>/dev/null)"
}

mkdir -p "$T/bin" "$T/state" || fail "mkdir"
ln -s "$B/store" "$T/bin/store" && ln -s "$B/fuse-hub" "$T/bin/fuse-hub" &&
	ln -s "$B/tools/fake-sensors" "$T/bin/cap-sonar" &&
	ln -s "$B/tools/fake-sensors" "$T/bin/cap-radar-left" || fail "symlinks"
for n in alert status-lcd cap-radar; do
	ln -s "$B/tools/fake-child" "$T/bin/$n" || fail "symlink $n"
done

# ---- phase 1
"$B/dlby-super" 2>"$LOG" &
super=$!
for n in store fuse-hub alert cap-radar cap-radar-left cap-sonar; do
	wait_for "^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I first_heartbeat name=$n " "$LOG" 3000 ||
		fail "no first_heartbeat for $n"
done
order=$(sed -n 's/^dlby-super\[[0-9]*\] I child_start name=\([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' "$LOG" | head -n 7 | tr '\n' ' ')
[ "$order" = "store fuse-hub alert status-lcd cap-radar cap-radar-left cap-sonar " ] ||
	fail "start order: $order"

# fuse-hub crash: a new hub must be up within 1 s (§6 E restart).
hub=$(pid_of fuse-hub "$LOG")
t0=$(date +%s%N)
kill -SEGV "$hub" || fail "kill -SEGV fuse-hub"
wait_count '^fuse-hub\[[0-9]+\] I start ' "$LOG" 2 2000 || fail "fuse-hub did not restart"
t1=$(date +%s%N)
restart_ms=$(((t1 - t0) / 1000000))
[ "$restart_ms" -le 1000 ] || fail "fuse-hub restart took ${restart_ms} ms (> 1000)"
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] E child_exit name=fuse-hub signal=SEGV$' "$LOG" ||
	fail "no child_exit name=fuse-hub signal=SEGV"
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I child_restart name=fuse-hub in_ms=100$' "$LOG" ||
	fail "no child_restart for fuse-hub"

# Sonar data keeps reaching store through the new hub.
s1=$(sonar_records)
sleep 1.5
s2=$(sonar_records)
[ -n "$s1" ] && [ -n "$s2" ] && [ $((s2 - s1)) -ge 15 ] ||
	fail "sonar records after hub restart: $s1 -> $s2 (want +15)"

# store killed outright: restarted.
st=$(pid_of store "$LOG")
kill -KILL "$st" || fail "kill -KILL store"
wait_count '^store\[[0-9]+\] I start ' "$LOG" 2 2000 || fail "store did not restart"
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] E child_exit name=store signal=KILL$' "$LOG" ||
	fail "no child_exit name=store signal=KILL"

# alert crashed by itself at 1 s: restarted.
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] E child_exit name=alert signal=SEGV$' "$LOG" ||
	fail "no child_exit name=alert signal=SEGV"
wait_count '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I child_start name=alert ' "$LOG" 2 2000 || fail "alert not restarted"

# cap-radar hung at 1 s: heartbeat lost after 5 s, TERM ignored, KILL, restart.
wait_for '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] W child_kill name=cap-radar signal=KILL$' "$LOG" 9000 ||
	fail "cap-radar was not killed"
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] E heartbeat_lost name=cap-radar$' "$LOG" ||
	fail "no heartbeat_lost name=cap-radar"
wait_count '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I child_start name=cap-radar ' "$LOG" 2 2000 ||
	fail "cap-radar not restarted"
wait_for '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I first_heartbeat name=cap-radar ' "$LOG" 3000 ||
	fail "restarted cap-radar never heartbeat"

kill -TERM "$super" || fail "super already gone"
wait "$super"
rc=$?
super=""
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dlby-super exited $rc"
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I exit code=0$' "$LOG" || fail "no clean exit line"
last=$(sed -n 's/^dlby-super\[[0-9]*\] [IE] child_exit name=\([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' "$LOG" | tail -n 1)
[ "$last" = store ] || fail "store was not the last child to stop (last: $last)"
for p in $(all_pids); do
	alive "$p" && fail "child $p outlived dlby-super"
done

# status-lcd exited 78: logged once, never restarted.
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] E child_exit name=status-lcd code=78$' "$LOG" ||
	fail "no child_exit name=status-lcd code=78"
grep -q -E '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] E child_disabled name=status-lcd code=78$' "$LOG" ||
	fail "no child_disabled for status-lcd"
[ "$(count '^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I child_start name=status-lcd ' "$LOG")" -eq 1 ] ||
	fail "status-lcd was restarted"

# Each fake child, first runs and restarts alike, inherited only 0-3.
nfds=$(count '^(alert|status-lcd|cap-radar)\[[0-9]+\] I fds open=' "$LOG")
[ "$nfds" -ge 5 ] || fail "want >= 5 fds lines, got $nfds"
bad=$(grep -E '^(alert|status-lcd|cap-radar)\[[0-9]+\] I fds open=' "$LOG" | grep -v 'open=0,1,2,3$')
[ -z "$bad" ] || fail "leaked fds: $bad"

sum=$("$B/tools/dlby-logcat" "$DLBY_LOG_DIR") || fail "dlby-logcat: $sum"
[ "$(field bad "$sum")" -eq 0 ] && [ "$(field contiguous "$sum")" -eq 1 ] || fail "store log: $sum"

# ---- phase 2: super dies by SIGKILL; the children must follow.
"$B/dlby-super" 2>"$LOG2" &
super=$!
for n in store fuse-hub alert cap-radar cap-radar-left cap-sonar; do
	wait_for "^dlby-super\[[0-9]+\] I first_heartbeat name=$n " "$LOG2" 3000 ||
		fail "phase 2: no first_heartbeat for $n"
done
pids2=$(sed -n 's/^dlby-super\[[0-9]*\] I child_start name=[^ ]* pid=//p' "$LOG2")
kill -KILL "$super" || fail "kill -KILL super"
wait "$super" 2>/dev/null
super=""
i=0
for p in $pids2; do
	while alive "$p"; do
		i=$((i + 1))
		[ "$i" -gt 50 ] && fail "child $p outlived a killed dlby-super by > 1 s"
		sleep 0.02
	done
done

cat "$LOG" "$LOG2" | grep -q -E 'AddressSanitizer|LeakSanitizer|runtime error' && fail "sanitizer report"

echo "super_e2e: ok (hub_restart_ms=$restart_ms sonar=$s1->$s2 $sum)"

# Plan: cap-radar and cap-sonar (M3 blocker)

## Context
M3 needs both real sensors flowing through the real pipeline (capture -> fuse-hub -> store).
Hub, store, super and fake-sensors exist; src/capture/ is empty. Pi smoke test
(docs/evidence/pi-sensor-smoke.txt) proved UART2 frames and kernel-timestamped echo edges.

Contract (DEMO.md §3A, hb.h, msg.h): ipc_conn_init(&c,"fuse-hub"), memset-zeroed
radar_msg/sonar_msg via ipc_send, hb_init once + hb_tick/hb_readable every loop pass,
exit 0 on SIGTERM or super gone. super runs children with no args -> config by env.

## Decisions
1. GPIO via raw kernel uAPI (<linux/gpio.h> v2 ioctls), not libgpiod: no new dependency,
   and the kernel edge-event path is the mechanism we cite in DESIGN.md §2.
2. Radar sends ntargets=0 for every frame until a real target capture verifies the layout.
   Non-empty frames are counted and hex-logged (rate limited). Decoder is a follow-up.
3. Sonar sends nothing when the sensor gives no edge at all or sticks high: the hub counts
   any SONAR message as alive (fuse-hub.c:203-213 ignores flags), so staying quiet is what
   makes the hub's 8-ping staleness mark it lost. Echo wider than 25 ms (4.3 m) is sent
   with SONAR_NO_ECHO (sensor alive, nothing in range).
4. mlockall attempted, warn-and-continue on EPERM (unprivileged bench runs). FIFO
   priorities stay with dlby-super's existing TODO (Jackson).
5. Two-pod --side deferred (needs msg.h + hub + super changes). Env config makes a second
   instance a config change on our side.

## Files
- src/capture/radar_parse.{c,h}: pure byte-sync frame parser (header F4F3F2F1, u16 LE
  len, tail F8F7F6F5, max len), counters for bad length/tail.
- src/capture/cap-radar.c: open $DLBY_RADAR_DEV (default /dev/ttyAMA2) raw 115200 8N1,
  O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOCTTY, tcflush; poll {tty, hb fd}; origin_ns = read time;
  one radar_msg per good frame. Logs: radar_up, radar_silent (no frame 3 s), radar_back,
  bad_frame (limited). Exits: 78 bad config / ENOENT, 69 read EIO, 0 SIGTERM/super gone.
- src/capture/echo.{c,h}: pure classifier: edges + trigger time -> OK(echo_ns, rise_ns) |
  OUT_OF_RANGE | NONE | STUCK.
- src/capture/cap-sonar.c: $DLBY_SONAR_CHIP (/dev/gpiochip0), TRIG 23 out, ECHO 24 in
  both edges, event buffer 16; timerfd CLOCK_MONOTONIC TFD_TIMER_ABSTIME 60 ms; poll
  {timerfd, edge fd, hb fd}. Each tick: classify previous ping, send, drain, 10 us trigger.
  Logs: sonar_lost reason=no_echo|stuck_high (8 pings), sonar_back, overrun (limited).
  Exits: 78 bad config / ENOENT, 69 EBUSY, 0 SIGTERM/super gone.
- tests/test_radar_parse.c, tests/test_echo.c: unit tests (split frames, junk, bad
  tail/length, back-to-back frames; width math, >25 ms, no rising, stuck).
- tools/fake-ld2451.c + tests/capture_e2e.sh: pty-backed fake radar -> real cap-radar ->
  fuse-hub -> store; check radar records, bad=0, bad_frame logged, SIGTERM exit 0;
  cap-sonar with a missing chip exits 78.
- Makefile (shared): CAP lib, build/cap-radar + build/cap-sonar in PRODUCT, capture_e2e
  in run-tests. Mirrors existing rules.

## Verification
On the Pi: make, make test, make asan (show output). Then hardware: cap-sonar standalone
vs a taped distance; cap-radar with the hub; DEMO.md run with real children; unplug
radar -> `degraded lost=radar`; disconnect ECHO -> `sonar_lost reason=no_echo`.
Commits: "M3: ..." on gagebranch, PR to main.

# Don't Look Behind You: team rules

## Context
A car-mounted device that warns a driver of a cyclist in the right-side blind
spot before a right turn (the "right-hook"), fusing a rearward radar and a
sideways ultrasonic sensor under a supervisor that survives any child process
dying. Latency and on-device autonomy are
graded properties, not preferences — see Hard constraints below. Background
and design rationale: PROBLEM.md. No implementation exists yet (no Makefile,
no src/ tree); the Commands and Ownership sections below describe the target
layout to build toward.

## Commands
- Build: ‘make‘ Cross/deploy: ‘make deploy PI=pi@<host>‘
- Tests: ‘make test‘ Sanitizers: ‘make asan‘ Valgrind: ‘make memcheck‘
- Soak sanity: ‘make soakcheck‘ (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- A change is DONE only when build, test, and asan pass. Show output.

## Hard constraints
- The PRODUCT makes no network calls except serving its own LAN
interface. No LLM APIs, no cloud inference, no pretrained models.
The intelligence in src/hub/ is ours. This is a graded boundary.
- Every daemon must be supervisable: clean exit codes, no orphaned
fds across restart, heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall’s error path handled and
logged. The 48-hour soak is the test suite of last resort.
- NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.

## Ownership
One folder per process:
- src/common/ (msg.h, ipc, log): shared
- src/capture/ (cap-radar, cap-sonar): Gage
- src/hub/ (fuse-hub): Jackson
- src/store/ (store): Jackson
- src/super/ (dlby-super): Jackson
- src/alert/, src/lcd/ (alert, status-lcd): Jackson
- tests/: unit tests. tools/: Python, bench and replay tooling, never deployed.

- Gage: capture pipeline, sensor pod, bench sketch
- Jackson: fusion, storage, supervisor, alert and LCD, replay harness
- Shared: src/common/, 48h soak, demo, evaluation report.

The agent edits outside the current session owner’s area only when told explicitly whose
session this is.

## Style
- Systems core: C17, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, no VLAs.
goto-cleanup for multi-resource functions.
- Python permitted only under tools/. No graded mechanism
may live there.
- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Workflow
- Multi-file or algorithmic change: plan first, wait for approval.
- Hardware bugs: paste real evidence (dmesg, timing capture,
/proc/interrupts). No fixes proposed from a verbal description.
- Commit only from a green state; message format "M<n>: <what>".

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.
